engine.text: Every body is rigid. All give is in the contact between the piece and a surface.
The trial's piece and any others the trial lists are the only free bodies.

A tube, a box with boxes cut out, a prism and a pie slice are run as their true convex pieces. Any other hollow, cut or imported solid is used as its convex hull; the record lists which, and says when the piece touched one.
MuJoCo finds where shapes overlap and moves the bodies. The forces there are this library's spring, damper and friction law, the same as the planar engine's.
Where a piece touches one surface at several points, the surface's spring is shared among the points by depth.
A moved group follows its motion and a driven surface runs at its drive's speed; contact loads the drive's motor model but cannot push a mechanism off its motion.
A roller, wheel or belt that a drive turns is a still shape whose surface runs at the drive's speed across the turn's axis.
A group whose motion is not one hinge or one slider is carried along its path without its speed being felt in contact.
A flap is its drawn solid on a sprung hinge about the plane's normal; its stops do not bounce.
A ring piece is a closed chain of straight round segments; the record says how many.
With more than one piece, piece against piece takes the one material the trial names; only the trial's own piece is reported contact by contact.
Custom forces are not run by this engine yet; a trial that has them is refused.
No air drag or lift.
Time moves in fixed steps; the half-step repeat is the check on the step.
